title: Running the right program is not enough for consciousness

statements.text: Computation alone is not enough for consciousness: a digital computer that behaves like a person, or simulates a brain, is not thereby conscious as the person is.

sources.quote: IIT implies that digital computers, even if their behaviour were to be functionally equivalent to ours, and even if they were to run faithful simulations of the human brain, would experience next to nothing.
classical digital computers are incapable of creating causally significant experiences
challenging the assumption that computation provides a sufficient basis for consciousness
real artificial consciousness is unlikely along current trajectories, but becomes more plausible as AI becomes more brain-like and/or life-like
Critical of the viewpoint of ‘strong artificial intelligence’ (‘strong AI’), according to which all mental processes are entirely computational
As such, the challenge to artificially create individualized consciousness becomes synonymous with the challenge to artificially induce abiogenesis.
